value.rationale: A complete exact terminal law on GP(10,2), the smallest fullerene and a canonical 20-vertex cubic lattice substrate, is a reusable finite benchmark for random sequential dimer adsorption. The strict stochastic-order comparison to the uniform maximal-matching null model quantifies a 7.761-fold kinetic perfect-coverage bias and is a genuine model-dependent phenomenon: an explicit connected six-vertex counterexample rules out any automatic general dominance. Known saturation and perfect-matching counts are not counted as contributions. The finite fact is self-contained and naturally motivated, without pretending a thermodynamic-limit theorem.
